content: 1. Pexidartinib: If the concurrent use of UGT inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the dose of pexidartinib as per the dosage modifications outlined in the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 2. Cobicistat: This drug increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 3. Phenobarbital: This drug decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for a lack or loss of virologic response to cobicistat. 4. Phenytoin: Similar to phenobarbital, phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for a lack or loss of virologic response to cobicistat. 5. Pimavanserin: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. 6. Pirtobrutinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Once the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued for five half-lives, resume pirtobrutinib at the previous dose. 7. Pomalidomide: Atazanavir increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Ponatinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the starting dose of ponatinib to 30 mg daily. 9. Posaconazole: This drug increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Pralsetinib: Both atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Primidone: This drug decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 12. Quetiapine: Atazanavir increases the levels of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for adverse reactions. Refer to the prescribing information for quetiapine for further guidance. 13. Rabeprazole: This drug decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to reduced plasma concentrations. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) should not exceed a dose comparable to omeprazole 20 mg and must be taken approximately 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naive patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 14. Ranolazine: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 15. Red Yeast Rice: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is chemically identical to lovastatin, and may increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 16. Repotrectinib: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3–5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 17. Resmetirom: Both atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of resmetirom. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of resmetirom, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 18. Ribociclib: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Rifampin: This drug decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 20. Rifapentine: This drug decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Rimegepant: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Riociguat: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of riociguat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Romidepsin: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Rivaroxaban: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration due to the increased risk of bleeding. 25. Rosuvastatin: Atazanavir increases the levels of rosuvastatin by an unknown mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Limit the rosuvastatin dose to 10 mg/day to reduce the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 26. Ruxolitinib: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg BID in patients with a platelet count ≥100 x 10^9/L and concurrent use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid use in patients with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 27. Salmeterol: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration due to the risk of cardiovascular effects, including QT prolongation, palpitations, and sinus tachycardia. 28. Selpercatinib: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If use is unavoidable, reduce the selpercatinib dose from 120 mg BID to 40 mg BID or from 160 mg BID to 80 mg BID. Wait at least 3–5 half-lives of the discontinued drug before resuming the previous selpercatinib dose. 29. Saxagliptin: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Selumetinib: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. 31. Silodosin: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 32. Siponimod: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of siponimod with a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor. 33. Sirolimus: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 34. Sodium Bicarbonate: This drug decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Sodium Citrate/Citric Acid: Similar to sodium bicarbonate, this combination decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Solifenacin: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Sonidegib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Sotorasib: This drug decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or refer to the prescribing information for dosage modifications. 39. Sparsentan: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or interrupt treatment with sparsentan if unavoidable. 40. St. John’s Wort: This herbal supplement decreases the levels of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 41. Sunitinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Stiripentol: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Suvolexant: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of suvolexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Tadalafil: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or adjust the tadalafil dose for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) or erectile dysfunction (ED) as per the prescribing information. 45. Talazoparib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of talazoparib. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
